All other countries, China (mainland-born) and India each moved up 365 days (≈12.0 months) to Oct 22, 2015. Mexico advanced 14 days (≈0.5 months) to Jul 15, 2001. The Philippines was unchanged at Jul 22, 2006.
USCIS says family-sponsored applicants must use the Dates for Filing chart (Table B) for Form I-485 this month.

sections.heading: F3 Final Action Dates moved up 365 days for three areas
paragraphs: Final Action Dates (Table A) show when a green card can be approved. For F3 in November 2026, All other countries, China (mainland-born) and India share the same date: Oct 22, 2015. In October 2026 it was Oct 22, 2014, so each advanced 365 days (≈12.0 months). That is the largest move in this category this month.
Mexico advanced from Jul 1, 2001 to Jul 15, 2001, a move of 14 days (≈0.5 months). The Philippines stayed at Jul 22, 2006, with no change from October 2026.

sections.heading: F3 Dates for Filing (Table B) and the I-485 this month
paragraphs: For November 2026, USCIS says family-sponsored applicants must use the Dates for Filing chart (Table B) to file Form I-485. If your priority date is earlier than the Table B date for your category and country, you may be able to file your adjustment of status application this month. Other eligibility requirements still apply.

F3 Table B dates for November 2026: All other countries, China (mainland-born) and India are each Nov 1, 2015, up 365 days (≈12.0 months) from Nov 1, 2014. Mexico is unchanged at Dec 1, 2002. The Philippines is unchanged at Oct 22, 2006.

sections.heading: How far Table B is ahead of Table A for F3
paragraphs: Table B dates are later than Table A dates. For All other countries, China (mainland-born) and India, Table B is 10 days (≈0.3 months) ahead of Table A. For the Philippines, Table B is 92 days (≈3.0 months) ahead.
Mexico has the widest gap in this category this month. Its Table B date (Dec 1, 2002) is 504 days (≈16.6 months) ahead of its Table A date (Jul 15, 2001).

sections.heading: F3 Final Action Date record over 6 and 12 bulletins
paragraphs: This record covers Table A only. For All other countries, China (mainland-born) and India, the date went from Feb 15, 2012 (since May 2026) to Oct 22, 2015, a net +1345 days (≈44.2 months). It advanced in 4 of the last 6 bulletins and was unchanged in 2. Over the last 12 bulletins (since November 2025), it went from Sep 8, 2011 to Oct 22, 2015, a net +1505 days (≈49.4 months). It advanced in 6, was unchanged in 6 and did not retrogress.

Mexico went from May 1, 2001 to Jul 15, 2001 over both periods, a net +75 days (≈2.5 months). It advanced in 3 of the last 6 bulletins and was unchanged in 3. Over 12 bulletins it advanced in 3 and was unchanged in 9.

The Philippines went from Nov 22, 2005 to Jul 22, 2006 over the last 6 bulletins, a net +242 days (≈8.0 months), advancing in 2 and unchanged in 4. Over 12 bulletins it went from Sep 22, 2004 to Jul 22, 2006, a net +668 days (≈21.9 months), advancing in 6 and unchanged in 6. It did not retrogress in either period.
